[[File:Patricia Lewis (9914623843).jpg|thumb|300px|Patricia Lewis 2013 at [[Heinrich-Böll-Stiftung]] in Berlin]]
'''Patricia Lewis''' (born 1957) is a British and [[Irish people|Irish]] [[nuclear physics|nuclear physicist]] and [[arms control]] expert, who is currently an independent consultant. She was previously: the research director for international security at [[Chatham House]].<ref>Nuclear disarmament: Thinking outside the silo, https://www.chathamhouse.org/publications/the-world-today/2021-04/nuclear-disarmament-thinking-outside-silo</ref>; the senior scientist-in-residence and deputy director at the [[James Martin Center for Nonproliferation Studies]] at Monterey Institute of International Studies (MIIS); the director of the [[United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research]] (UNIDIR) and the director of [[VERTIC]].

==Biography==
[[File:Aston Webb Hall, Birmingham University.jpg|thumb|right|150px|[[Birmingham University]]]]
A dual national of Ireland and the United Kingdom, Lewis holds a BSc in physics from the University of Manchester and a PhD in nuclear structure physics from the [[University of Birmingham]]. Dr Lewis also holds an Honorary Doctor of Laws from the University of Warwick (2015)<ref>https://warwick.ac.uk/services/gov/hongrads/list/</ref>. In 1982, she was a special assistant in the Rehabilitation Centres for Children in [[Kolkata]], India, and from 1983 to 1986, she lectured in physics at the [[University of Auckland]], in New Zealand, from where she also carried out research at the Australian National University in Canberra, and she was a visiting lecturer at Imperial College London. during her tenure at VERTIC.

From 1986 to 1989, Lewis was information officer of the London-based VERTIC [[Verification Technology Information Centre]], and its director from 1989 to 1997. She was the director or the United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research (UNIDIR) in Geneva 1997–2008<ref>[[United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research]]</ref>{{Circular reference|date=August 2026}}. She was deputy director and scientist-in-residence at the James Martin Center for Nonproliferation Studies at the Monterey Institute of International Studies, California from 2008 to 2012.  Lewis was a Commissioner on the WMD (Blix) Commission, an advisor to the Evans-Kawaguchi [[International Commission on Nuclear Non-proliferation and Disarmament]] (ICNND) and a member of the Ekeus Advisory Panel on Future Priorities of the OPCW.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.opcw.org/media-centre/news/2010/12/new-advisory-panel-future-priorities-opcw-holds-first-meeting-hague#:~:text=The%20panel%20is%20chaired%20by,industry%2C%20and%20science%20and%20technology. | title=New Advisory Panel on Future Priorities of the OPCW Holds First Meeting in the Hague }}</ref>. She was co-director of the Global Commission on Internet Governance 2014–2016.<ref>Final Report of the Global Commission on Internet Governance , https://www.cigionline.org/publications/one-internet/ </ref>. She currently sits on the Stockholm International Peace Institute (SIPRI)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sipri.org/about/organization/board |title=Governing Board &#124; SIPRI }}</ref> and the EEAS Space Advisory Board to the Special Envoy for Space<ref>https://www.eeas.europa.eu/eeas/space_en#6151</ref>. Lewis is currently the co-chair of the Scientific Advisory Group for the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons<ref>https://www.icanw.org/tpnw_scientific_advisory_group</ref>,<ref>The Scientific Advisory Group for the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons and Its Statement on the 80th Anniversary of the Nuclear Weapon Era, Lewis P. and Mian Z., 2025, The Journal of Peace and Nuclear Disarmament, Vol 8 (2) 2025, P451-457 https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/25751654.2025.2583006?src=</ref>

==Career==
During the 1988–90 negotiations on the [[Treaty on Conventional Armed Forces in Europe|CFE treaty]], Lewis was a consultant to the British [[Foreign and Commonwealth Office]] on the verification of conventional force reductions in Europe.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20000918093004/http://www.utdallas.edu/dept/socsci/prog%20pg16.htm Arms and Disarmament: A Woman’s Issue], University of Texas at Dallas</ref>

In 1989–90 Lewis was appointed British government expert to the United Nations study on the Role of the United Nations in Verification.<ref name="unidirauthors">{{cite web |url=http://www.unidir.org/pdf/ouvrages/pdf-3-92-9045-168-8-en.pdf |title=Archived copy |accessdate=2006-03-15 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20060207150019/http://unidir.org/pdf/ouvrages/pdf-3-92-9045-168-8-en.pdf |archivedate=7 February 2006 }}</ref> From 1990 to 1992 she was a visiting Lecturer at [[Imperial College London]] and was the 1992-3 Elizabeth Poppleton Fellow at the [[Australian National University]].{{citation needed|date=June 2024}}

She was chair of the UK Gulf Syndrome Study Group<ref>https://meselsonarchive.hsites.harvard.edu/sites/g/files/omnuum7261/files/meselsonarchive/files/199528_cwcb28.pdf </ref>. She was also an external reviewer for the [https://web.archive.org/web/19970712074241/http://www.dfat.gov.au/cc/cc_report_mnu.html Canberra Commission Report on the Elimination of Nuclear Weapons], and a member of the Tokyo Forum for Nuclear Nonproliferation and Nuclear Disarmament 1998–99.<ref name="tokyoforummembers">{{Cite web |url=http://www.fas.org/news/japan/report-m.htm |title=The Report of the Tokyo Forum for Nuclear Non-Proliferation and Disarmament |access-date=15 March 2006 |archive-date=24 October 2004 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041024030909/http://www.fas.org/news/japan/report-m.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> From 2004 to 2006, Lewis was a commissioner on the Weapons of Mass Destruction Commission<ref>The Weapons of Mass Destruction Commission, https://www.wmdcommission.org/</ref>, chaired by [[Hans Blix]]. Currently Lewis was an advisor to the International Commission on Nuclear Non-proliferation and Disarmament (ICNND).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.icnnd.org/|title=International Commission on Nuclear Non-proliferation and Disarmament|website=icnnd.org}}</ref> Lewis served on the [[American Physical Society]]'s Panel on Public Affairs (POPA) study on Technical Steps to Support Nuclear Arsenal Downsizing"<ref>{{cite web |url=http://cns.miis.edu/other/lewis_patricia_100200_nucleardownsizing.pdf |title=Archived copy |accessdate=2010-03-25 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100407155846/http://cns.miis.edu/other/lewis_patricia_100200_nucleardownsizing.pdf |archivedate=7 April 2010 }}</ref>

Lewis was the recipient of the 2009 American Physical Society Joseph A. Burton Forum Award for her contributions to the public understanding of science in arms control and international security<ref>The American Physical Society, Joseph A. Burton Forum Award, https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/award/burton-forum-award</ref> and received Ireland's Presidential Distinguished Service Awards (2023) in January 2024 for her work on education, science, and innovation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://president.ie/en/diary/details/president-presents-the2023-distinguished-service-awards |title=Diary President Presents The2023 Distinguished Service Awards }}</ref>
